lyric: And I'm not cool and I'm not smart
lyric_idea: AI outscoring people: a PhD-level science benchmark (deck-first), a test built as the last exam for AI (deck-first), an AI IQ headline, and the 2023 bar-exam headline, with a counter-headline noted for the bar exam.

candidates.text: experts who have or are pursuing PhDs … reach 65% accuracy
candidates.speaker_or_outlet: Rein et al., GPQA paper (arXiv:2311.12022); pairing figure from ITWire (Alex Zaharov-Reutt)
candidates.deck_source: /home/user/poster/ai-safety-presentation/tools/slides_splash_extra.js (GPQA 36% to 96%, PhD experts 65-70%); /home/user/poster/ai-safety-presentation/tools/slides_capabilities.js (35.7% to 95.8%). No GPQA image in assets/research.
candidates.verified_how: Opened the arXiv abstract: 'experts who have or are pursuing PhDs in the corresponding domains reach 65% accuracy'; 'highly skilled non-expert validators only reach 34% accuracy'; 448 questions. Opened the ITWire article (page loaded): 'GPQA Diamond is 96%', published 4 Sept 2026, with the next sentence attributing the scorecard to OpenAI. The OpenAI scorecard itself was not opened.
candidates.why_it_fits: The only candidate that sets an AI score directly against a PhD baseline, which turns 'not smart' into 'AI outscores PhDs' on screen.
candidates.caveat: The 65% is the paper's full 448-question figure, while 96% is a Diamond score. These are different question sets, so label both. The deck's splash slide attributes 65-70% to GPQA Diamond experts, which the abstract does not support. The deck also gives 96% in one slide and 95.8% in another for GPT-6 Astra; the source opened says 96%. The 2023 expert figure is a human baseline; the 2026 score is a vendor-linked secondary report.

candidates.text: designed to be the last academic exam of its kind for AI
candidates.speaker_or_outlet: Scale AI and Center for AI Safety, Scale Labs Humanity's Last Exam leaderboard
candidates.date: Leaderboard page with the 17 Sept 2026 HLE-Rolling update; deck capture 2026-10-04
candidates.local_path: /home/user/poster/ai-safety-presentation/assets/research/capabilities/scale-hle-leaderboard.png (also aa-hle-leaderboard-oct2026.png and scale-hle-rolling-noise-ceiling.png in the same folder)
candidates.deck_source: /home/user/poster/ai-safety-presentation/assets/research/capabilities/manifest.json entries scale-hle-leaderboard, scale-hle-rolling-noise-ceiling, aa-hle-leaderboard-oct2026; tools/slides_capabilities.js hleSlide.
candidates.verified_how: Opened the labs.scale.com page (static text): '2,500 of the toughest, subject-diverse, multi-modal questions designed to be the last academic exam of its kind for AI'; 'developed in partnership with the Center for AI Safety'; top scores GPT 6 Astra 54.80±1.94 and Fable 5.1 (xhigh) 46.50±2.00 match the deck manifest. Opened the Artificial Analysis HLE page: Claude Opus 5.5 (Max, Default Fallback) 61.4% on 2,158 text-only questions.
candidates.why_it_fits: Puts the 'last exam' framing on screen with a live top score, so the lyric's 'not smart' reads as an exam AI is now passing.
candidates.caveat: Weakest fit to 'outscoring people': the page shows no human baseline. Scale (2,500 questions, full set) and Artificial Analysis (2,158 text-only) are not comparable, so never put both in one frame. The 64.4% no-tools Opus 5.5 figure is vendor-run (system card).

candidates.text: OpenAI's o3 scores 136 on Mensa Norway test, surpassing 98% of human population
candidates.trim_option: OpenAI's o3 scores 136 on Mensa Norway test…
candidates.verified_how: Opened the page (loaded): headline verbatim; 'OpenAI's new o3 language model achieved an IQ score of 136 on a public Mensa Norway intelligence test'; 'While o3 posted a 116 on the Offline evaluation, it saw a 20-point boost on the Mensa test'; figures attributed to TrackingAI.org. Opened trackingai.org/home (loaded): no scores listed, so the 136 and 116 figures are not confirmed on TrackingAI's own page.
candidates.why_it_fits: The most literal 'not smart' echo: an IQ number for an AI, in one headline.
candidates.caveat: Unofficial: independent tester data, and no official Mensa position was found. The Mensa Norway test is public, so contamination is possible; the offline score was 116. Alternate headline: TechRadar, 'AI took a huge leap in IQ, and now a quarter of Gen Z thinks AI is conscious' (page title read; body truncated; date not verified).

candidates.text: Latest version of ChatGPT aces bar exam with score nearing 90th percentile
candidates.trim_option: Latest version of ChatGPT aces bar exam… with score nearing 90th percentile
candidates.verified_how: Opened the ABA Journal page (loaded): headline, byline 'By Debra Cassens Weiss', and date 'March 16, 2023, 1:59 pm CDT' read verbatim; body truncated, so the model name is not confirmed from this page. Opened the arXiv abstract for the GPT-4 Technical Report (submitted 15 Mar 2023): 'passing a simulated bar exam with a score around the top 10% of test takers'.
candidates.why_it_fits: Matches the brief's event directly: GPT-4 passing the bar exam in 2023.
candidates.caveat: Contested. A 2024 paper by Eric Martinez (AI and Law) argues the 90th-percentile estimate is overstated (from a search summary; not opened). Counter-headline, opened: Live Science, 'GPT-4 didn't ace the bar exam after all, MIT research suggests — it didn't even break the 70th percentile | Live Science' (headline read; byline and date not verified). The 298/400 score in the search summary was not checked against the report body. The ABA headline does not name GPT-4.

deck_flags: slides_splash_extra.js labels 'PhD experts score about 65-70%' as GPQA Diamond. The GPQA abstract's 65% is the full 448-question set; no Diamond expert figure was verified.
GPT-6 Astra GPQA: slides_capabilities.js says 95.8%, slides_splash_extra.js says 96%; the ITWire article says 96%.
HLE: Scale (full 2,500 set) and Artificial Analysis (2,158 text-only) figures are not comparable; keep them in separate frames.
